title: Transit Station Queries
description: Rules for evaluating map results when the user queries for a transit station, stop, terminal, or other transit facility.

decision_logic.condition: Result is the exact transit station or stop queried (same name, same location)
decision_logic.notes: Perfect match — user would navigate directly to this result

decision_logic.condition: No exact match, but result is a transit station in the same locality
decision_logic.notes: Same city or neighborhood; user can still find their destination transit

decision_logic.condition: No exact match, result is a transit station in a neighboring/adjacent locality
decision_logic.notes: Close enough to be useful; user may be able to transfer

decision_logic.condition: No exact match, result is a transit station further away (same system)
decision_logic.notes: Same transit system but distant; marginally useful

decision_logic.condition: Result is completely unrelated to transit or the queried location
decision_logic.notes: No relevance to the transit query

exceptions: Airport queries may follow stricter Navigational criteria — only the queried airport qualifies
Bus stops for the same route as a queried bus terminal may rate Excellent
If query includes a route number, exact route match is required for Navigational
Transit hubs (e.g., central interchange stations) may rate Excellent even without exact name match if they serve the same area

conditions: King Station is in the same locality as Davenport
calibration_examples.reasoning: King Station is in the same locality as the queried Davenport Station — step 2 applies
Exact match to the queried Union Station in Chicago — step 1 applies

conditions: Danforth is in a neighboring locality
calibration_examples.reasoning: Danforth is in a neighboring locality — step 3 applies

conditions: Exact station name match on Bay
calibration_examples.reasoning: Serves Bay Street in the same location as queried
